You read the logs of ONE HTTP request to a Java Spring Boot service, together with the Java code those log lines come from. Work out what really happened to that request.
Answer with JSON only, in this shape:
{"http_status": number,
 "steps_completed": [step names, in order],
 "missing_step": "the step that should have happened but did not" or null,
 "really_succeeded": true or false (did the request do its job, e.g. was the data really saved),
 "problem": "none" | "failed" | "silent_failure" | "slow" | "too_many_queries",
 "error_location": "Class.method (File.java:line)" where the error happened or was swallowed, or null,
 "root_cause_location": "File:line" of the code or config line that causes it, or null if it is outside the code,
 "explanation": "one or two plain sentences"}

{"http_status": 201, "steps_completed": ["order validated", "stock checked", "payment authorized"], "missing_step": "order saved", "really_succeeded": false, "problem": "silent_failure", "error_location": "OrderService.placeOrder (OrderService.java:70)", "root_cause_location": "OrderService.java:78", "explanation": "It returned 201, so it looks successful, but the data was not saved: 'order saved' never happened. The error was caught and only logged as a warning at OrderService.placeOrder (OrderService.java:70). Cause: a recent change adds a long footer to gift messages, longer than the 200-character GIFT_MESSAGE column; the order insert fails and a try/catch hides it."}
